$comment: The issue catalog: one index over every open item in this repo, and the
only place that knows they are the same kind of thing.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Open work was tracked in four registers that had never been
counted together: PLAN.md's numbered follow-ups (the roadmap of record),
backlog.md (unscheduled optimization), each design doc's open-questions
section, and validation/ledger.json (the checks a machine cannot run). Each
register was internally disciplined and none could see the others. The cost
was not theoretical: page-turning.md OE9 was found only because somebody
opened that document and read to the end, and nothing anywhere would have
noticed if it had been fixed in code and left marked `confirmed` in prose.
WHAT IT IS NOT. This file does not restate an issue. It carries no title, no
description, no reproduction — those live in the document that owns the item,
and a copy here would drift while still looking authoritative. That is the
same rule validation/ledger.json runs on and the same reason map.json points
at symbols instead of quoting them. What this file adds is the metadata no
single document can hold: severity, who owns it, what it blocks, what closed
it, and the fact that two registers are describing one item.
HOW A SOURCE IS READ. Every design doc under docs/design/ ends with a section
headed exactly `Open questions, and what would answer each`, and backlog.md's
body is one such register. Under both, an item is a heading of the form
### OEn <title> · **status**
so scripts/gate-issues.mjs finds items without knowing anything about the
document. `status` in this file must equal the marker in that heading; the
duplication IS the gate, in the same shape as the SOURCES.md <-> Colophon.tsx
licence-copy check.
TWO SOURCES ARE READ DIFFERENTLY, ON PURPOSE.
validation/ledger.json is already machine-readable and already gated. Its
checks are indexed here by id and their status is read from the ledger, not
copied — gate-validation.mjs stays the authority on them.
PLAN.md's follow-ups are NOT marked. They are compound narratives whose job
is to record how a thing was believed over time — follow-up 2 keeps its own
retracted licence claim beside the correction, and 10 carries three
successive re-measurements. Flattening one of those to a single word would
destroy the thing it is for. So a PLAN follow-up is indexed by number, the
gate checks only that the number still exists, and this file's `status` is
the summary rather than a checksum. That is the one special case and it is
written down rather than discovered.
STATUS VOCABULARY. Six words, defined once, here.
open       nobody has decided; no blocker named
confirmed  a defect, reproduced, with the numbers in its source
suspected  read from the code, never reproduced or profiled
blocked    the next step is named and unavailable (hardware, a hafiz, a loop)
answered   decided; nothing owed in code
fixed      closed in code AND in a test that would fail if it came back.
`closedBy` is required and the gate refuses the word without it —
the same standing rule the ledger runs on, that a result must
tighten something automated or it has not been banked.
SEVERITY. Three words. `defect` — the app does something wrong today.
`question` — a decision not yet made. `risk` — something unmeasured that
could be wrong, which is the category `suspected` items live in.
FIELDS
id         kebab slug, stable, referenced by blockedBy
source     {file, item} — a design/backlog OEn row, a PLAN follow-up number,
or {ledger: <check id>}
status     see above; must match the source marker except for ledger/PLAN
severity   defect | question | risk
owner      agent (doable from this machine) | user (needs a human or hardware)
blockedBy  ids in this file, ledger check ids, or a loop name
closedBy   required when status is `fixed`: the test or gate that notices a
regression. A path, and the gate checks it resolves.
make issues        the open items, grouped, worst first
make issues-doc    regenerate docs/issues.md (a gate checks it is not stale)
pnpm gate:issues   the invariants
the `issues` skill drives triage: pick, open, close

The headline claim was overstated — ctrl+wheel always fired — and the register keeps the wrong sentence beside the correction. The calibration argument is left standing because it was correct about what it measured; the binding is gone, ctrl+wheel is now swallowed, and nextWheelTurn is reused verbatim for a Shift+wheel juz jump. The plain-wheel half — the actual headline of this item — is untouched. decisions/wheel-and-zoom.md.

No new string was needed for the skip, as the item predicted. The ends did need one: firstPage/lastPage now carry the page number, because 'last available page' alone leaves a reader guessing which of 604 they stopped at.

The proposal was reviewed and taken whole, Escape included — PageDown/PageUp give a way to turn, Escape gives a way back to the arrows. The ladder did not move: rule 3 still beats both, which is what keymap.test.ts is really asserting.

Deleted, not wired: page-transition.md §3.1 withdrew the cross-fade in favour of the fold, whose rule is that no glyph moves during a turn. 'answered' rather than 'fixed' on purpose — a test asserting the absence of a CSS rule proves nothing, so there is no test to name.

The one item in that document never reproduced — it carried `suspected` for six loops rather than borrowing a confidence it had not earned, and it was closed by a test rather than by the profile it asked for. Its own measurement was still never taken; what changed is that the heading's claim is now false. Owned by backlog ③; indexed twice here on purpose, because two registers describing one item is exactly what this catalog exists to make visible.

Curiosity, not a blocker — SS4.6 fixes it constant here regardless. But if the reference does vary it, that is a design it got wrong for a memoriser.

±1. The arrow turns a page, at every width. The behaviour is unchanged and every reason for it is new: §6 argued from scarcity (±2 over an inventory of three is a no-op) and loop-4b deleted that argument. What holds now — stepPage must name any landing that is not the page next door, so ±2 would announce a correction on every turn (page-turning.md §7 ④); ±2 reaches one parity only, putting half the print out of reach of the arrows, for the reader with the fewest ways back to them; a keyed turn, a wheel turn and a dragged fold all end in one stepPage and would stop meaning the same thing; and appKeyAction would have to learn the window's width, which KeyContext deliberately cannot see. What made ±2 attractive — half the presses on a spread move no paper — is not a defect: both leaves of the opening are already open, and PageStage:855 already suppresses the fold for it. Reasoning is in keymap.ts; the pin is desktop.spec.ts's 'still turns pages with the arrow keys the header advertises', which reads 8 after one press and would read 9 under ±2.

Neither: above default zoom the book closes to the one leaf being read. The question offered two ways for two leaves to behave under a zoom and the reader reframed it — a spread is an offer of more of the book at once, and zooming is declining that offer in favour of one page. Panning was already answered and nobody had noticed: holdAxis centres any axis that fits, so at z<=1 a pan is a measured no-op. Three defects the running app had, found by screenshotting it rather than reading it: a cold ayah link left the two leaves at different scales (1.55 vs 1.0) with the selection band cut by the gutter; ctrl+wheel over the facing leaf zoomed the facing leaf, so hover was silently choosing the subject of the gesture against decision row 15; and a third — that zoom pushed the fore-edge outside the clip — was claimed from the screenshots and is FALSE, measured: ::after is inside the transformed host and travels with it, so at 2.07x the whole host sits inside the book's box. It thickens with the page, which the border does too and PageStage.module.css argues for. No issue filed; the wrong claim is kept beside the measurement in desktop.md. The shared View was rendered rather than argued about and reads as one continuous column, which an opening is not. The size argument for closing was WRONG and is kept beside its correction: .leaf is height-bound at ~398px whether one leaf or two are on the desk, so this buys no reading size — it buys the viewport, a page at 1.55x seen whole instead of through a 398px slot. Built as onFitChange on PageStage (flip, not frame; z <= 1+1e-3 because a tween's last frames arrive at 1.0000003) plus solo on PageSpread as style and not mount, and a ResizeObserver on the stage layer because the leaf now widens because of a zoom. Decision row 23. STILL FIXED, MECHANISM SUPERSEDED: the answer above survived and the way it was built did not. Deriving soloLeaf from zoom leaked three ways — ctrl+wheel over the facing leaf took it to 1.549 alone while the live leaf sat at 0.8 (the comment saying the facing leaf 'never receives a gesture that could change its own scale' was simply untrue, and is why nobody looked); a breakpoint crossing remounted the live stage and reset its view but not the mode, leaving data-solo=true over scale(1); and atFit's z <= 1+1e-3 against MIN_ZOOM 0.8 reopened the book at 266px beside 332px. One state with two owners has patches, not a fix. Page mode is now an explicit radiogroup and zoom an explicit stepper, disabled while the book is open — the same finding kept as an ordering of two controls instead of a derivation. onFitChange and atFitRef are deleted; the ResizeObserver stays, for the independent reason recorded here. Decision rows 25-27, decisions/wheel-and-zoom.md.

No. Landscape iPads (1194x834, 1080x810) clear the breakpoint on both axes and have no keyboard, so the item's trigger — wait for a bug report — was never going to fire. The hints alone gained (any-hover: none); the spread and the language switch stay on the breakpoint, because their premise really is room. any-hover over pointer:fine because iPadOS keeps touch primary with a Magic Keyboard attached. Still a proxy: no media feature reports a keyboard.

loop-4b dropped off the blocker list by happening: the second mount is real on every spread now, which is what made the risk measurable rather than hypothetical. It still cannot be answered without the on-device verdict, so the chain is one link shorter and not shorter than that.

Asked as a design question and answered as a defect: RevisionMap was the only one of eight sheets with no `@media (min-width: 900px)` rule, and at 1440px its auto-fill grid laid 30 juz out as a single row. Fixed with a bounded centred card plus a named column count per scope; the owed row in docs/decisions/desktop-vs-mobile.md is row 22.
A ledger candidate. The bands decide what `cold` means, and a threshold chosen by whoever wrote the renderer is a claim about somebody else's revision habit.

Answered by building it. A held cell is a button that opens its division on the lowest page of it this build holds — read off the manifest through the same scopesOf sweep that decides whether the cell is drawn, never off HIZB_STARTS, which knows the ayah and not the page of this print. coverage became holdings and returns a map instead of a set. The announcer says «الحزب ٣ · صفحة ٢٢» at hizb and juz scope and nothing extra at page scope, where the cell and the landing are one fact. An absent cell stays a plain li with no control at all. The grid is one tab stop, not 604, via a roving tabindex — and page-scope cells meet WCAG 2.5.8 by the equivalent-control exception (the jumper), not by size.

Latent rather than hypothetical: one edition is vendored, but an IndexedDB record outlives the build, so stored page ids would join the next print's grid silently. comparableEvents partitions at page scope only — a juz is the same in every print, and filtering there would show a hafiz less revision than they did.
37 forms Arabic silently substitutes today. One JSON edit each, but the edit needs a hafiz's eye. Named in its source as a known defect, deliberately deferred.

`I18n.other` deleted; both switches now render LOCALE_IDS from LOCALES. Behaviour-preserving at two locales — the registry's order is the order the hand-written buttons were in — so it was done without a third locale to render blind at. LOCALES gained `abbr` for the header. Tests in i18n.test.tsx and DesktopChrome.test.tsx are written over LOCALE_IDS, so they fail the day ur.json lands.

A real limit of interpolation, not a defect: the repair for a locale that inflects the inserted name is a different message, authorable only by someone who speaks the offering language. Narrowed by ④ — each button now interpolates its own name rather than `other`'s, so only the surrounding grammar is still at issue. §⑦'s checklist is where a new locale meets it.

FIXED 2026-08-07, the same day it was opened, and by three more corrections beside it. alef-madda is now an entry in CORRECTIONS with respell [[/أٓ/g, 'ءَا']] — three codepoints where the print spends two — and the inference this row flags as unread was confirmed the only way it can be: the oracle went UP rather than down. On its own it takes the residual from 143 ayahs to 60. The same onset windows, re-read after it, gave tatweel-carrier (172 → 143, and a last 12 → 11 for the rare noon carrier), small-madda (60 → 19) and hamza-below (19 → 12). Together with the three structural corrections: 97.03% → 99.81%, 172 residual ayahs → 11, and paintability moved unasked (past-the-end 2 → 0, wider-than-two 4 → 1), which is the second and independent reason to believe them. The narrowness is measured rather than chosen — generalising the tatweel rule to every U+0640 scores 94.48%, WORSE than applying nothing. Closed by tajweed-fold.test.mjs, which pins each of the four both ways: with the correction on the span width matches the identity fold, with it off it does not, so deleting a respell fails a test rather than quietly moving an aggregate. Worth keeping from the original note: the inspector published the finding and the bake wrote the rule, so the number is evidence rather than the tool grading its own homework. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. Opened 2026-08-07 by probe-encodings.mjs on its first full pass, and it is the first thing the inspector found that nothing else could. The fold's residual is not scattered: offsets are cumulative, so one divergent codepoint pushes every later annotation in its ayah by the same amount, and 166 of the 172 residual ayahs carry exactly ONE delta throughout. That property makes the window between the last oracle hit and the first miss a localiser, and the words standing in those windows are one orthographic family — ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ in 41 of the 41 ayahs it appears in, ٱلۡأٓخِرِ 16/16, ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ 9/9, ٱلۡأٓيَٰتُ 3/3, ٱلۡأٓخِرَ 3/3, لَأٓتِيَةٞ 2/2, every window bounded on both sides, every delta −1. All of them contain U+0623 ALEF WITH HAMZA ABOVE + U+0653 MADDAH ABOVE: the print spells أٓ in two codepoints where the text the tajweed offsets index spells it in three. That is 275 of the 475 misses, 57.89%, in one shape. What this does NOT have is the other side of the comparison — Tanzil's spelling is in a text this repo does not hold, so 'three codepoints' is inferred from arithmetic and not read. Two smaller families are visible in the same table and are the same kind of claim: U+0640 TATWEEL + U+06E7 SMALL HIGH YEH at +1 (ٱلۡأُمِّيِّـۧنَ 3/3, يُحۡـِۧيَ 2/2, إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ 6 ayahs), and U+06E4 SMALL HIGH MADDA (يَسۡجُدُۤ 3/3, ٱسۡجُدُواْۤ 3/3). Worth recording separately: the +1 bucket had been attributed to the tatweel before this tool existed, on the strength of U+0640 occurring 535 times in the corpus, and the onset table says the bucket is heterogeneous and the tatweel is a minority of it — a plausible untested attribution corrected by the first run. What would answer it is a fourth entry in CORRECTIONS and a re-run; the oracle is the referee, because a wrong expansion makes it WORSE rather than silently better. Left to whoever owns the tajweed bake — the inspector's job is to show what is true, not to be right.

ANSWERED 2026-08-07, and the answer is no — it was correction 5 arriving, not the source. Measured on both folds rather than reasoned about: on the three structural corrections there are 90 lam_shamsiyyah misses of which 21 begin on ٱ, across 19 ayahs, reproducing this row exactly; on all seven there are 7 misses of which ONE begins on ٱ, at 36:52, which probe-tajweed-words.mjs's NAMED list already carries on other grounds. So the observation was sound and the attribution was not: those 19 ayahs are ٱلۡأٓخِرَة / إِبۡرَٰهِـۧم territory throughout, and what looked like a span starting one letter early was the أٓ drift already accumulated by the time the fold reached them. Nothing is owed upstream and nothing is owed in the bake. The lesson outlasts the row and is why it is kept rather than deleted: a drift of exactly one letter reads as an off-by-one in whoever wrote the span, because that is the most available explanation and it points away from your own code. The only thing separating it from the true reading is re-measuring under a different correction set — which is exactly what alef-maddah-is-a-fourth-correction's toggle mechanism bought, and the reason the corrections are a parameter rather than an edit. Before filing any future finding as upstream, switch corrections off and watch whether it grows. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. 21 lam_shamsiyyah annotations across 19 ayahs (2:124, 2:126, 2:127, 2:130, 2:132, 2:136, 2:213, 2:260, …) miss the oracle at +1 with the drift shape exactly ٱ — the source's span begins on the alef wasla rather than on the ل the rule is named for. Suspected upstream in tajweed.hafs.uthmani-pause-sajdah.json rather than in the fold, because the same rule lands correctly on the alignment everywhere else and because these are all ٱل + a sun letter. Not confirmed: it would take reading the source's raw entries for those 19 against controls where the rule lands right, which the inspector's drill-down makes one click of work. If it is a source defect the fix is a named exception list in the bake, in the shape segmentation.mjs already uses for its four orthographic exceptions — NOT a widened oracle, which would buy coverage by making the check unable to see the next one.

FIXED 2026-08-07. All eighteen rules are in ORACLE; coverage is 60057/60057 = 100.00% of annotations and the hit rate is 59975/60057 = 99.863%, 82 misses across 10 ayahs, every one named. The widening was done the way this row said to do it — each letter set written from the tajweed rule FIRST and measured second, never read off where the offsets happened to land — and each entry carries the reason it has its shape in a required `why` field a test asserts is non-empty. The row's own warning was borne out twice. `iqlab` written as the high meem U+06E2 alone scored 85.05%, a reject by this repo's criterion; the 84 unreachable misses all had the shape «ِۭ ب», because the mark is written LOW (U+06ED) under a kasra and HIGH over a fatha or damma. With both it is 562/562 — the oracle catching its own letter set, which is precisely the failure this row named. And the headline number needed a companion: a hit rate alone is not evidence, because breadth is free — {ا,و,ي} is ~12% of the corpus, so a rule restricted to it would score well on a fold that was simply wrong. `oracleDensity(cps, rule)` measures what fraction of positions in an ayah would have satisfied the rule; 1 − density is the chance the check notices a one-codepoint drift, and both probes now weight by it. Sensitivity-weighted the coverage is 93.65%, not 100%, and `madd_6` (fifteen letters, 30% of the ayahs it appears in, 69.6% sensitivity, 148 annotations) says in its own `why` that it is the entry to distrust. Two sets were then corrected BY the residual rather than the reverse: ikhfa gained U+06E8 SMALL HIGH NOON (نۨجي writes the hidden noon small) and silent gained ص (the sin/sad alternate, where the letter written is not the letter read, which is what silent means). Both are marked data-led in their own `why`, because they were added after the residual pointed at them rather than written blind like the other sixteen, and the fix for a fit is to say so rather than hide it. The widening also paid the dividend this row doubted it would: correction 8, `sakta-seen`, is a substitution that was measured and REJECTED under the two-rule oracle (worth 1 annotation, 0 ayahs — 36:52 in probe-tajweed-words' NAMED) and is worth three ayahs under the eighteen-rule one, because silent, qalqalah, madd_246 and idghaam_shafawi had no vote when it was first weighed. ORIGINAL NOTE FOLLOWS. The oracle checks two of the source's eighteen rules — hamzat_wasl must start on ٱ, lam_shamsiyyah on ل — because those are the only two naming a letter whose identity is not in doubt. That is 15,985 of 60,057 annotations, 26.6%, and the headline 99.81% is 99.81% OF THAT QUARTER; the other 73.4% inherit a verdict they cannot witness. Several remaining rules have nearly characteristic letters (qalqalah on ق ط ب ج د, idghaam_ghunnah on ي ن م و) and admitting them would raise coverage a lot. Deliberately not done yet, and the reason is that widening is measurable rather than arguable: add a candidate to ORACLE with its letter set and read the hit rate — one that lands at the incumbents' ~97% is witnessing alignment, one that lands at 60% is witnessing its own bad letter set, and a bad letter set degrades the instrument at exactly the job it exists for. Only worth doing when the existing residual stops being enough to find corrections with, and ① is evidence it has not stopped. UPDATED 2026-08-07: ① was answered by four corrections read straight out of that residual, so the seam it was mined from is now 11 ayahs and 30 misses rather than 172 and 475. That strengthens the case for widening — an eighth correction has far less to be read off — without touching the argument against it, which is unchanged: a wrong letter set degrades the instrument at exactly the job it exists for. Still open, and now open for a better reason than when it was filed.

ANSWERED 2026-08-07: the caller came, and the boundary moved by exactly the distance this row proposed — outlines yes, ink no. Section ① now draws the ayah's word boxes from assets/words/hafs-kfqc/<page>.json on the same frame the app uses, with the rest of the page behind them faintly and a toggle for it; no glyph is drawn and nothing is read from assets/pages/**. The line §6.4 actually protects turned out not to be 'draws nothing' but 'makes no claim about appearance', and a rectangle out of a gate:words-checked shard makes none. Three things were settled before anything was drawn, and each of them shaped the result. (a) Every one of the 6,236 ayahs has from === 1 — an ayah's boxes are never split across two shards — so print word i is boxes[i - 1] unconditionally; readBoxes ASSERTS that rather than assuming it, because a non-1 from would shift every label silently and look fine. (b) A box is tinted on its HOST index, not its print index, so a word the fold dropped is a gap on the page exactly as it is a gap on the codepoint ruler — that is what makes the two panels one instrument rather than two pictures, and it is why clicking a box selects the annotation over it and lights the ruler in step. (c) When the box list and the data-hafs word list disagree on count the view draws the geometry and REFUSES to number it, warning with both counts, because the failure it would otherwise produce is word 7's box under word 8's label. LICENSES.md buckets apps/web/public/assets/adj/** under 'Free use with attribution (inherited) — Waqar144's', naming the mutashabihat dataset alone. So the shipped adjacency shards carry values COMPUTED FROM GPL'd data, and under the same strict reading of 'derivative' this repo applies to itself elsewhere they are a GPL derivative with one of their two parents unnamed. Independent of Track B and wrong today, which is why it is `confirmed` rather than parked with the rest of that document's rows. It matters more inside a store binary than on the web, and the asymmetry is the point: a static site discharges GPL §4–6 by handing the browser the whole bundle, which is LICENSES.md's own argument for plain GPL over AGPL, while a wrapped binary is the thing that has to be licensed. What would answer it: correct the row to name both parents, and decide whether gate:license-copy's reach should extend to the bucket table — the drift here was introduced by a FEATURE rather than by anyone touching a licence file, so the gate that would have caught it is one that notices an asset tree gaining a new upstream.

Track B's blocker is a licence Hifth does not own. A GPL'd binary on Apple's App Store conflicts with the per-device and DRM terms GPL §6 and §10 do not let a distributor add; the projects that ship anyway (Signal, OsmAnd) do it by having EVERY copyright holder grant an additional permission under §7. Hifth cannot assemble that grant. The Quranic Arabic Corpus header — quoted verbatim in SOURCES.md and pinned into the colophon by gate:license-copy — grants the GPL and then says copies may be distributed but 'CHANGING IT IS NOT ALLOWED'; SOURCES.md already records that tension and resolves it for a website by vendoring verbatim and deriving at build time, but a §7 additional permission IS a change to the licensing terms and only the copyright holder can grant it. quran-tajweed's CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(5)(B) separately forbids applying Effective Technological Measures, which FairPlay is — narrower, because the skin is one edition and could be omitted from a store build, where the QAC-derived data cannot (see adj-shards-have-two-upstreams). And KFGQPC's own terms are still unread by a human (board item #55), which a store submission is exactly the context that stops making deferrable. All of this is argued from licence text by a non-lawyer, and 'I read the licence' is not the standard this repo holds gates to. What would answer it: a licensing opinion from someone qualified, scoped to the three upstreams by name. Until then Track B stays gated and docs/design/track-b-native.md stays the reason.

The runnable half of nobody-has-looked-at-the-placement-verdicts: that row is the question, this row is the twenty minutes that answers it. Built 2026-08-08 — `pnpm adjudicate:marks` renders a hundred blind two-panel trials over forty pages, and `pnpm adjudicate:score` rebuilds the key from the seed afterwards, so nothing on disk knew the answers while they were being given. Deliberately a forced choice rather than a list of verdicts with agree/disagree beside each: a person shown a machine's verdict agrees with it, and what comes back is the machine's own opinion wearing a human's name. It is a risk rather than a question because mark-C cannot ship on an uninspected correction. Wired into `make session CHECK=placement-correction-by-eye` on 2026-08-12: opened from a session the trials post each answer straight into that sitting's transcript and bank the ruling file at the end, so the twenty minutes cannot end in a download nobody can find. Still says nothing about how it is going, because it still does not know.

The other half hour, and it asks a question the first one cannot. A forced choice returns a preference — our rectangle beat the one it was shown against — and a correction that points the right way and falls a third short wins every trial while still being wrong. Built 2026-08-12: `pnpm nudge:marks` renders one rectangle per trial, starting a fixed distance out in a direction that changes every time, and the reader puts it where it belongs; `pnpm nudge:score` subtracts what the machine proposed from where it was actually put, and what is left is a magnitude in units. It reports that against the reader's OWN precision, measured in the same sitting from marks shown twice, because a residual smaller than the hand that produced it is not a finding. Deliberately a second session rather than a drag handle on the first: adjusting a rectangle inside a two-panel trial and then scoring the landing against the two starting positions IS the answer key, and adjusting after answering teaches the direction of the correction, which points the same way on nearly every page. The two should not be worked back to back by the same person. Risk rather than question because mark-C's thresholds are a claim about magnitude and only this can check one.

The placement measurement has been reproduced twice and its controls hold, but no human has looked at a single verdict. Until one does, the thresholds in that document's §⑦ stay unenforced and nothing is wired into CI. What replaced it is a forced choice between two rectangles with nothing on screen saying which is ours and no key written down until the scorer rebuilds it from the seed; it carries its own controls (obviously-wrong rectangles to catch a session worked while distracted, identical pairs to catch a person who always picks something, and same-size displacements in other directions to measure whether an eye can resolve a shift this small at all — which is what the headline number has to be read against). Scoped 2026-08-12, which is a narrowing of what this row can ever deliver rather than of the work: a forced choice settles a preference and not a distance, so a-preference-does-not-say-how-far now carries the magnitude half and neither row's answer should be read as the other's.

Opened 2026-08-12 by building the instrument that answers it: a forced choice yields at most one bit per trial — is the proposed move preferred to the alternative it was shown against — so it can confirm a direction and is structurally incapable of confirming a distance, and every threshold in that document's §⑦ is a claim about distance. What answers it is a placing session: one rectangle, started deliberately out of position, put where a reader says it belongs, with the proposed correction subtracted from the landing afterwards. The runbook is `placement-residual-by-hand`. It ran the same day, over 60 marks placed by one reader, and this is what came back. SETTLED by it: the correction points the right way — 59 of 60 landed nearer the corrected rectangle than the shipped one (98.3%, interval 91.1–99.7), typical miss 1.15 units from the shipped box against 0.39 from the corrected one; the reader's own precision is 0.03 units, from 9 marks placed twice from independent starting points; the pull of where each rectangle started came out at effectively nil, which is what the evenly-spread starts were for; and 0/60 placements said the box was the wrong size. NOT settled, which is why this is open rather than answered: the residual of (-0.073 across, -0.110 down) is four times the precision floor, but the 60 placements sit on 40 pages and two marks on one page share that page's frame — clustered by page, neither component clears nought (down [-0.230, +0.009], across [-0.223, +0.077]). It was marginal before that correction and is not established after it; most of the interval is still on one side, so our correction MAY be short. Recorded first as 'only the down component is separable from nought' and corrected 2026-08-12 when the scorer was taught to cluster; the lesson already existed in probe-mark-ink.mjs about its own sampling and had not travelled. Nor could the sitting measure the correction's SIZE at all: the 40 pages propose nearly the same move, so 'exactly right' and 'a fifth short' produce the same landings and the gain spans from the wrong sign to 2.5x. More trials do not fix that — see the-correction-is-only-judged-where-it-was-fitted, which is also why every placement so far came from a page the correction was fitted to, and which since closed its coverage half: all 604 pages are now measured, they vary far more widely than those 40 did, and the leverage this section lacked therefore exists. Verdict, therefore: adopt the correction as measured, do NOT apply the residual. Applying it would edit the recorded per-page displacements rather than the arithmetic that derives them, is the-displacement-correction-could-go-stale's neighbour, and is tracked as mark-C — but it is not to be done on this evidence. Ruled out along the way and worth not re-buying: not the mark's name (a mean per name leaves MORE spread, 0.425 vs 0.415 down and 0.545 vs 0.526 across, over 11 names), not a scale error across the page (t = -0.5 down, -1.6 across), not the starting point, not fatigue (t = 0.2 down, -0.5 across against trial order). What would close this: a sitting on held-out pages, several marks per page so the page and the hand can be told apart, and a second reader — disagreement over 0.03 units would make the residual a fact about a person rather than about the print. This is not nobody-has-looked-at-the-placement-verdicts' answer either: a distance and a preference are scored separately and never summed.

Opened 2026-08-12 as 'only forty pages have a measured correction'; renamed the same day when the coverage half was closed and the name stopped being true. WHAT IT ANSWERED: the corrections do vary, and the first 40 pages hid it. Those 40 were representative in the centre — their mean correction is indistinguishable from the other 560 (t = -0.1 across, -1.2 down), which was not guaranteed — but understated the spread badly (page-to-page sd 0.107/0.097 against 0.172/0.165 over the rest), and most of what spread they did show was measurement noise: scoring the same 40 pages twice from different mark samples disagrees by about as much as those pages differ from each other. That is precisely why the sitting built on them could confirm direction and never size. The variation is also not the same on both axes: 95% of pages need a downward move inside the original range, so down behaves nearly like one global number, while only 51% fall inside the original across range, about nine pages need essentially NO across move while needing the usual down one, and page 113 wants to move the opposite way down from every other page. WHAT THAT UNBLOCKS: the original 40 offered a 0.31-unit span of proposed moves, nearly all noise, which is why a-preference-does-not-say-how-far came back undecidable on size; across all 604 that span is over 1.75 units, so a sitting drawing marks from both extremes gets several times the leverage per placement — enough to tell 'exactly right' from 'a fifth short', which no number of placements on the original 40 could have done. The zero-across pages and page 113 are worth the most, being where one-number-for-the-print and one-number-per-page disagree loudest. STILL OPEN, and the reason this row is: no reader has judged a single mark on a page outside the original 40. Every by-eye placement to date came from a page the correction was fitted to, because a trial needs a proposed move to start from. Only a held-out sitting separates a fit from a finding, and it can be built now. ALSO MEASURED, and new: taking each page's own displacement out is most of the repair and measurably not all of it — separation -0.234 to +0.281, marks beating their own null 13.5% to 75.7%, but 19.49% still further than 0.75 units off afterwards and a corrected median overlap of 0.492 against the 0.909 a per-mark best fit reaches. Whatever that remainder is, it is not a page-level shift, and it is NOT the same quantity as the leftover distance in a-preference-does-not-say-how-far — that one is a further move of the correction, this one is scatter the correction cannot reach. Neither is applied. Both shift files are now committed under docs/validation/rulings/ so a banked verdict re-derives from committed bytes.

Does each page carry the number of marks of each name the text says it should, in that order? Counting is blind to geometry and geometry is blind to counting: no score in either document can see a missing or duplicated mark, because a mark that was never drawn has no box to be wrong about. Cheap next to everything else here.

Answerable only once placement is corrected, because it needs to know where the letter is. Carried here only — mark-labels.md §⑦ Option D points at this row rather than repeating it.
